translations.text: say it, nor did they believe the one who first told them
“Do not let those who live in Judea rejoice.”
For the one whose identity they do not know is looking into the distance, ready to stamp his sandal down upon those in Idumaea and those who practice deceit in its midst with filthy pleasures.
[?] like the one about whom it was said, “For honey drips from the lips of a prostitute; afterward you will find her bitter as wormwood.”

Was it not because of those who were afflicted by this sickness, or whom this sickness afflicted, that anguish weighed upon the prophets from the beginning like a stone, as they said, “They destroyed my life in a pit; they put a stone over me. Water poured over my head. I said, ‘He has abandoned me.’”
You will repay them with suffering according to the strength of their hearts.
O you alone, God, whose works are all truth and righteous judgments, who know the distress of this sickness that has put my poverty to the test!
Oh, woe to you, those who have destroyed their virginity and their worth among you, and have defiled their endurance or the works of their endurance!
Wrath, anger upon anger, curse upon curse, judgment and bloodshed upon judgment and bloodshed, upon the heads of those who do or will do these wicked deeds among you at any time!
Likewise, mercy upon mercy, blessing upon blessing, grace upon grace, power upon strength, upon the heads of those who do or will do righteous deeds among you at any time!
Or in what way is that expression, “Repay” or “Take vengeance,” excessive compared with the many such things I have said in my anguish,
which I said while you listened, brothers, in the place where we sat on the mountain outside the assembly, near the rock or the wall?

For I sent for you again today so that you would understand that anguish is bitter, just as you saw its bitterness increasing around the place about which I told you that God had not spoken to me, so that no one would again think beyond what he hears me say.
